likely-worth-it: correctness benefit established by tests or linked issue evidence
likely-not-worth-it: material performance cost confirmed by non-advisory evidence
a tested lower-cost implementation or validated workaround preserves required correctness
unclear: evidence is incomplete, advisory-only, conflicting, or lacks a tested alternative

requires: correctness benefit established by tests or linked issue evidence
current cost does not clearly justify blocking the fix
confirmed material regression or high-confidence hot-path regression
regression is accidental or a viable lower-cost approach is identified
confirmed regression is not suppressed by unrelated coverage gaps
decision-relevant evidence is missing, stale, incomplete, sampled-only, static-only, or device-required
a concrete supported measurement path exists
no confirmed blocking regression already determines optimize-before-merge
sealed executed-validation artifact identifies the workaround
workaround validated on every affected platform
framework-fix cost is measured and likely not worth it
human triage remains responsible for issue disposition
evidence supports competing correctness, performance, compatibility, or maintenance concerns, or no supported measurement path exists

hardGates: Keep empirical verdict separate from recommended next action.
Do not calculate a synthetic worth-it score.
Use unknown when a factor is not established by evidence.
Do not invent an absolute cost, execution frequency, affected scope, or expected percentage benefit.
Incomplete or advisory-only evidence cannot support likely-worth-it or likely-not-worth-it.
A plausible-unverified workaround cannot drive merge or issue-disposition advice.
Validated requires a sealed executed-validation artifact, established affected scope, and correctness tests on every affected platform; accessibility remains not-assessed unless explicitly tested.
Never recommend automatic issue closure and expose no issue-closing capability.
